title: An effect can be saved as a named style
goal: A colour can be saved under a name, and now so can the way a piece of text is set. The third kind the spec asks for is missing: a shadow, a glow, a blur or a border somebody has spent time tuning cannot be kept under a name, so putting the same drop shadow on eight cards means setting eight shadows by hand and changing them means changing eight.
notes:
Third of the three style kinds in docs/design/ui-building.md. Do it the way the other two do it: Sources/PhotonzCore/ColorStyles.swift and Sources/PhotonzCore/TextStyleLibrary.swift are the two working examples, and the text one is the closer model because an effect, like a text treatment, is several values kept together rather than one. Same shelf, same reconcile-on-every-edit rule, same LinkBreaks kind. Flag: next-styles.

The hard part the other two did not have: an effect lives at a PLACE in the Effects list, and the list moves (Layer.insertEffect/removeEffect/moveEffect already remap colour bindings by index). Decide early whether the binding names the place or the effect.
acceptance: An effect in the Effects list can be saved under a name from its own row
The saved effect appears on the Library Styles shelf beside the saved colours and text styles
Adding that name to another layer gives it the same effect, and editing the name changes every layer wearing it in one undo step
A row wearing an effect style says so and still answers, the way a colour row and a text row already do
